**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What's there:** Article III (p0048) is a purely one-way ownership clause — Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and "Derivative Work" (1.3) is defined broadly enough to capture any additions, modifications or enhancements built on the Platform. "Intellectual Property Rights" (1.6) is itself defined as rights *of Licensor* only.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** there is no statement anywhere that we retain rights in our own data (including the trade records, reports and error-diagnosis data we must generate and hand over under Article V.IV and Article VII(e)) or in our pre-existing IP; and the customization work we pay for under Article VII(b) (a "unique client front end") is a Derivative Work, so it vests in Licensor while we hold only a non-exclusive, Field-of-Use-limited licence for the term (renewal being at Licensor's option). No ownership and no perpetual licence-back.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** a single inserted carve-out after Article III — we retain our data and pre-existing IP with no assignment and no joint ownership; funded customizations are assigned to us, with Licensor retaining its pre-existing platform IP and granting a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Licensor IP embedded in them. Fallback offered in the comment: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the customizations instead of title.
- **Not flagged:** Licensor's ownership of the E-Path FX Platform itself, which is expected in a licence of this kind.
